title: Kernel Fingerprint Suite and Trace Sampling Protocol
abstract: This doc specifies a fingerprinting approach for kernel-level performance signatures and a reproducible trace sampling protocol for our runtime regression harness. The aim is to detect subtle regressions in kernel behavior, scheduler interaction, and KV cache effectiveness across quantization and batching changes.
purpose: Create a stable, low-noise benchmark suite that: 1) produces compact kernel fingerprints usable for quick comparison across commits and model builds, 2) defines how production traces are sampled and seeded into microbench runs so CI can catch regressions that matter in the wild.
scope: Covers: single-kernel microbenchcases, multi-kernel end-to-end fingerprints, trace stratification rules, KV cache warm/cold scenarios, scheduler interference scenarios (bursting, preemption), and regression detection heuristics. Does not cover long-running cluster-level scaling tests or cost-optimization experiments.
test-suite-overview: We split the suite into three layers: 1) Microkernel probes: tiny, deterministic workloads that isolate a kernel (attention, matmul, rotary, kv-read/write). 2) Fingerprint runs: composed workloads that run a deterministic sequence of tokens across typical beam sizes, batch sizes and kv-hit ratios to produce a compact per-run fingerprint. 3) Trace-replay scenarios: replay of stratified production trace segments through the full runtime including batcher, scheduler, and KV cache to measure system-level impact.
fingerprint-methodology: Fingerprint = vector of normalized metrics for a run: [p50-per-token-latency-ms, p95-per-token-latency-ms, kernel-invocations-per-token, memory-alloc-peak-MB, sustained-gpu-utilization-percent, kv-hit-rate, inference-throughput-tokens-per-s]. Each metric is normalized against a baseline run for the same model+hw and then scaled using median absolute deviation to reduce noise sensitivity. Fingerprints are hashed to a short id and stored in the benchmark DB with metadata (git commit, model, quantization, hw, driver versions, dyn batch config).
trace-sampling-protocol: We seed the trace corpus according to a stratified-sampling policy: strata = {short-prompts (<=64), medium (65-512), long (>512)} x {kv-warm (>=80% hits after priming), kv-cold (<10% hits)} x {single-concurrency, burst-concurrency (simulated 8-32 clients)}. For each strata we pick N segments per week (N depends on strata weight) using probability proportional to recent traffic volume but capped to keep total corpus < 2000 segments. Each sampled segment is anonymized (no user PII) and annotated with context-length distribution, token-entropy estimate, and observed client concurrency. The protocol requires maintaining a rolling 90-day window; older segments are sampled less frequently.
microbench-cases: List of representative microbench cases included: 1) attention-only: 1-layer, 128-head attention microprobe at sequence lengths [64,256,1024] 2) matmul-peak: dense matmul shapes aligned with model hidden dims for small/med/large models 3) kv-lookup-heavy: repeated KV cache lookups with varying hit ratios (0%, 50%, 90%) to exercise caching path and mem access patterns 4) quantized-decode: int8 and float16 decode loops measuring dequant overhead 5) kernel-consolidation: back-to-back small kernels to test launch overhead and scheduler packing. Each case includes a canonical input generator, warmup iterations, and 10k token steady-state window.
regression-detection-rules: A change is flagged if any of the following conditions are met in CI nightly or PR gating: a) p95-per-token latency increases by >6% AND absolute p95 increase >= 2ms, b) memory-peak increases by >8% or crosses model-specific safety thresholds, c) kernel-invocations-per-token deviates by >10% indicating scheduling regression, d) kv-hit effective throughput drops by >7% for same hit-rate synthetic runs, e) flaky runs where stddev across 5 repeats > 5% for p95. When flagged, the run produces a diagnostic bundle (trace, kernel timeline, nvprof summary, scheduler-sampling) and auto-opens a JIRA with links.
experiment-runbook: Nightly job: run fingerprint suite across target commits (main + last release) on matrices: hw=[A100-40g, H100, T4], model-sizes=[small,base,large], quant=[fp16,int8]. Store fingerprints and alert on regression rules. PR gating: quick fingerprint smoke (reduced strata) run on PR branch; if smoke flags, run full fingerprint in CI runner. Manual investigation steps: 1) compare fingerprint vector diffs, 2) isolate microbenchcase that changed, 3) enable kernel-level tracing with minimal trace length, 4) reproduce locally with same driver/kernel. Use run command: ./bench/run --suite fingerprint --model <m> --hw <node> --trace-corpus <path> --repeat 5 --out <artifact_dir>.
observability-metrics: Primary metrics saved per run: run_id, commit_sha, p50_ms, p90_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, tokens_generated, kernel_time_ms, host_time_ms, peak_gpu_mem_mb, avg_gpu_util_pct, kv_hits, kv_misses, scheduler_preemptions, batcher_batch_size_dist (histogram). All runs also produce flamegraphs and a kernel-invocation timeline (CSV) for quick diffing.
sample-results: Example fingerprint diff (abbreviated): baseline: p95=14.2ms, kernel-invocations=1.0, kv-hit-rate=0.88. PR-abc123: p95=15.7ms (+10.6%), kernel-invocations=1.12 (+12%), kv-hit-rate=0.87 (-1%). Flag triggered by p95 and kernel-invocations rules. Investigation traced extra kernel re-launches when quantized matmul took fallback path for sequences >512. Patch: adjust kernel selection predicate to prefer fused matmul when available; re-run shows p95=14.3ms.
outstanding-questions: 1) How to integrate on-prem hardware variants into nightly runs without exposing infra constraints? 2) Should we include a synthetic 'noisy neighbor' mode to simulate co-located tenant interference? 3) Where to draw the line between fingerprint dimensionality (more metrics = better signal vs storage/analysis cost)? 4) How to version fingerprint normalization so cross-model comparisons remain meaningful?
next-steps: 1) Land PR that implements fingerprint hashing and storage to benchmark-db (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pulls/482). 2) Implement trace anonymizer job and add it to infra pipeline (owner: Aisha). 3) Add a noisy-neighbor toggle to the trace-replay harness for Q2 experiments. 4) Run a 2-week backfill of the last 500 commits to establish historical baselines.
notes_to_reviewers: Focus review on the regression thresholds and the sampling caps — both are tuned for a compromise between signal sensitivity and CI cost. If you think thresholds should be more/less strict, annotate with suggested numbers and empirical justification. Also check linked PR and JIRA for existing infra work.
